title: No daemon-side embedding spend budget; runaway loops bill silently
wanted_capability: A daemon-side embedding budget guard: a configurable daily token or request ceiling per provider (and per route) that, once crossed, parks the affected routes in an explicit health state (health_reason=budget_exhausted, visible in bbox_embed_status and bbox_inbox) instead of continuing to call the provider. The 2026-08 incident re-embedded a never-converging ~51k-doc cohort every sweep for two weeks at roughly 50-60 USD/day on Voyage because nothing bounded provider calls and nothing surfaced the volume: the loop was only visible in the vendor's bill. A budget guard turns a runaway loop into a loud, cheap failure within a day. Counters already exist per route (indexed/retried/capped); the missing piece is a provider-call meter with a ceiling and a health trip.
missing_primitive: per-provider daily embedding call/token budget with route health trip
fallback_used: Sweeper disabled outright (BLACKBOX_EMBED_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS=0) and operator advised to set a vendor-side key cap.
evidence: Voyage billing: ~50-60 USD/day from 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-23, exclusively after the voyage-4 route migration went live
src/embed_runtime.rs residue sweeper re-enqueueing 3,591-51,593 docs per sweep with coverage never landing (gap-a7d80bb2)
